_comment: The real board, measured 2026-11-07: 53 x 53 mm squares. With the carriage at home (beside a8) the magnet's centre is at a8's centre along Y and 42 mm short of it along X, so as the Pi counts (home_beside a8 mirrors Y) a8's centre is 42,420, a1's 42,49 and h8's 413,420. Files run along +X, ranks along +Y. (Sketch 5's 52.5 mm squares were not the board that was built.)
_mm_per_turn_comment: Carriage travel for one motor turn, X and Y, measured on 2026-11-06 (one-turn buttons in the console). The firmware counts real mm with $100 = full_steps_per_turn x microsteps / mm_per_turn[0]; the Pi and the console send it on every connection. microsteps 1: the DRV8825 M0-M2 pins are not wired (full steps).
_magnet_home_comment: Where the magnet's centre sits on the sketch at home. 0,0: Sketch 5 already traces the magnet itself, so the magnet's 60 mm offset from the Y gantry's left edge is built into the sketch (it is why the frame is wider than the sketch). If the board check shows every square off by the same amount, change this (or use 'a1 is here' in the console).
_park_comment: The sketch has 17 circles a side, 24.7 mm apart, from y 12.35 to 407.65; the widest piece is 27 mm, so every other circle is a slot (9 a side, 49.4 mm apart).
_travel_comment: Sketch 5's far corner: the magnet travels 470 x 420 mm from home ($130, $131).
_docking_comment: No docking lanes: a person always takes captured pieces off (the gantry never removes pieces).
_step_pulse_comment: step_pulse_us, when set, is sent as $0 before each job (firmware 0.5+). Unset: the firmware's boot value, 1500 us (what moves the bench's motors; 333 steps/s, 68 mm/s at full steps with 41 mm per turn).
_home_beside_comment: Which square the home corner is next to on the real board (2026-11-07: a8). With a8 the Pi mirrors Y on the USB link, so everything else still counts a1 at y 26.25; see gantry_driver.y_flip_mm.
_camera_cal_comment: Camera calibration (console: Calibrate with camera). camera_cal_target 'piece': the magnet drags an ordinary chess piece (the camera photographs the empty board first, then finds the one piece on it); 'token' instead uses the optional printed ArUco token (id 10, console/token/README.md). camera_cal_piece_height_mm: the height of the piece you use, base to top: measure it (45 is a guess). A short, round, symmetric piece is best, a pawn or a rook. camera_hfov_deg: the camera's horizontal field of view, for the parallax of the piece's top.
_edge_routes_comment: Every carry: square centre -> one of its corners -> along the lines between squares -> a corner of the target square -> its centre, so it slides between the other pieces (board_paths.edge_routes).
_position_memory_comment: Home once: the Pi remembers the carriage's spot in ~/.duen-gantry/position.json (GANTRY_STATE_DIR overrides) whenever the board reports Idle and homed, and marks it 'moving' before every move. When the ESP32 restarts (port opened, supply dip, Pi reboot) the console's Connect and the touch app's next job put it back ($HM, then G92 to the spot) instead of asking for a home, unless the power went off mid-move, the motors were switched off (M18), there was an alarm, a stall or a stop mid-move, or steps/mm or home_beside changed. keep_esp32_running: open the USB port with DTR/RTS held low so the ESP32 does not restart at all (flashing with esptool/arduino-cli resets it as before). park_at_start_after_job: after each job the empty magnet goes to start_mm (a8's centre, from the camera calibration); only when start_mm is saved.
